findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: A two-cohort assay comparison found method- and antigen-dependent false-positive and false-negative anti-nephrin antibody results. Approximately half of 24 MCD samples had weak signals detectable only by immunoprecipitation-Western blotting; strong cross-assay signals occurred in two FSGS samples. This qualifies the comparability and specificity of human seropositivity estimates without negating experimental antibody effects.
findings.quote: Different assay methods and antigen preparations led to method-specific false-positive and false-negative results.
findings.studySystem: Human assay-method comparison across two cohorts totaling 169 patients and controls; 24 MCD and 63 FSGS samples; ELISA, IP-based ELISA, IP-WB and cell/tissue immunofluorescence.
limitations: Methodological assay comparison, not a controlled clinical causation study or a population-prevalence estimate.
Weak assay-specific signals do not establish pathogenicity; orthogonal confirmation and antigen quality matter.
findings.distinctFindingRationale: Separate cohort added following actual external summary feedback; not independent replication of multiple readouts from the same paper.
